constraints: Read both input files; join counts columns to metadata rows on sample ID and verify 6 anti-PD-1 vs 6 isotype control before any computation.

Quantify the depth disparity (library sizes, and sample_01 relative to median); include sample_01 in the main analysis but mark it for the downstream sensitivity analysis rather than silently dropping it.
Filter low-expression genes (e.g. keep genes with CPM > 1 in at least 6 samples); report gene counts before/after filtering.

steps.name: MCP-counter + EPIC deconvolution
caveats: mMCP-counter scores are relative units — a population can be 'higher in treated' without being 'more abundant in absolute terms'; EPIC fractions are compositional and confounded with tumor content.
EPIC TRef was built on tumor data; check that its output covers the stromal populations (CAF, endothelial) the question asks about — if not, note that stromal estimates come from mMCP-counter only.
Deconvolution from bulk assumes the reference populations are represented in these tumors; a poor cross-method correlation is a finding to report, not a bug to tune away.
steps.context: Consumes the TMM logCPM matrix and VST matrix from T1S1. Primary method: mMCPcounter (mouse MCP-counter) on the logCPM matrix — returns mouse immune AND stromal population scores (arbitrary units, valid for between-group comparison, not fractions). Second method: EPIC with the mouse TRef tumor reference (EPIC::EPIC(expr, reference="TRef")) on an expression matrix in a scale EPIC expects (non-negative, roughly log2-CPM or TPM-like; verify against package documentation and state the choice) — returns per-sample fractions including tumor/other cells and immune/stromal populations. Both methods use the mouse gene symbols already present in the counts matrix; verify identifier compatibility (symbol vs Entrez) against each package's reference before running and report any gene-loss from the join.
steps.question: What immune and stromal cell populations (CD8 T, CD4 T, NK, B, monocytes/macrophages, neutrophils, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, etc.) does each of the 12 subcutaneous tumors contain, estimated by two independent mouse-compatible methods whose shared populations can be cross-checked?
constraints: Run mMCP-counter on all 12 samples; emit a genes(sample) x population score table and the per-population marker gene set sizes actually used.

Run EPIC (TRef mouse reference) on all 12 samples; emit per-sample cell-type fractions; check fractions are non-negative and that within-sample cell fractions are consistent with EPIC's model (tumor/other fraction reported alongside).
Cross-method agreement: Spearman correlation between mMCP-counter scores and EPIC fractions for every population name both methods cover; report the matrix.
If one method cannot be run (reference mismatch, package API difference), report precisely why, proceed with the other, and mark the result as single-method.
Do not interpret or test treatment differences in this step — that is T3S1.
acceptance_criteria: Two per-sample composition tables (mMCP-counter scores; EPIC fractions) covering all 12 samples, with population names, method units, and the sample_01 flag carried in the output.
A cross-method Spearman correlation table for shared populations with a plain-language note on agreement.
A short methods note stating the EPIC input matrix and reference used, and the mMCP-counter marker-set coverage of the filtered gene set.

steps.name: Ortholog-projected TME signature scoring
caveats: Human-to-mouse ortholog projection loses markers and can shift specificity; this view is corroborative, and disagreements with T2S1 should be reported, not reconciled by hand.
The staged scGate signatures were built for gating single-cell data; using them as bulk signatures is an approximation — say so in the methods note.
steps.context: Consumes the TMM logCPM matrix from T1S1. Marker sets come from the staged scGate human TME gating signatures (/mnt/refs/managed/scgate-human-tme/v0.17/master_table.tsv, human gene symbols, '-' suffix marks negative markers) plus the per-population model files beside it. Convert human signatures to mouse 1:1 orthologs with babelgene, intersect with the 12,000-gene filtered matrix, and score per sample with UCell (rank-based, robust to library size and to the sample_01 depth disparity). This step only enriches the analysis — if ortholog coverage or the staged signatures are unusable, report that and stop without failing the run.
steps.question: Do the tumors differ in canonical TME marker-signature activity (T cell, NK, myeloid, B, fibroblast, endothelial, checkpoint-bearing populations) as scored gene-set-wise — a third, marker-based view independent of both reference-matrix deconvolutions?
constraints: Parse master_table.tsv: split semicolon-separated markers, strip the trailing '-' from negative markers and keep the sign; expand per-population signature membership from the model files if needed.
Project each human signature to mouse via babelgene 1:1 orthologs; report per-signature coverage (projected markers / input markers) and drop signatures below 50% coverage with a note.

Score with UCell on the logCPM matrix for all 12 samples; emit a sample x signature score table; if a scored signature's distribution is degenerate (e.g. all-zero due to gene loss), report it rather than imputing.
No group testing here — T3S1 consumes these scores.
acceptance_criteria: A sample x signature UCell score matrix for all 12 samples with the signature gene-set sizes and ortholog coverage fractions recorded.
Explicit statement of which signatures were dropped and why, or an explicit 'all signatures scored' statement.
UCell's size-factor robustness is noted as the reason this step is robust to the sample_01 depth caveat.

steps.name: Treatment-contrast statistics on composition
caveats: 6 vs 6 gives no power for interaction-level claims; any 'responder vs non-responder' framing is out of scope — there are no response labels in the metadata.
MCP-counter scores and UCell scores are not fractions: between-group comparison is valid, absolute-abundance language is not.
A single batch and no covariates beyond condition means the model is condition-only; do not invent covariates.
steps.context: Consumes all three composition outputs from T2S1 and T2S2 (mMCP-counter scores, EPIC fractions, UCell signature scores) for 12 samples, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch. For each population/signature: Welch two-sample t-test and exact Mann-Whitney U on treated vs control; effect sizes (Hedges' g and Cliff's delta) with bootstrap 95% CIs (e.g. 10,000 resamples); BH-FDR across populations within each method's table. EPIC fractions are compositional — additionally logit-transform cell fractions before testing and report both. Sensitivity: repeat all tests excluding sample_01 and flag any population whose direction or significance changes. Heatmap of the z-scored composition matrix with samples annotated by condition, and a summary table of populations consistently changed across methods.
steps.question: Which immune and stromal populations differ between the 6 anti-PD-1-treated and 6 isotype-control tumors, by how much, and is the pattern robust to the low-depth sample_01?
constraints: Test every population/signature from every method table; no cherry-picking — the BH-FDR scope is the full population set per method.

With n=6 vs 6, report effect size with CI first and p-values second; explicitly state that the study is powered only to detect large effects and that nominal (unadjusted) results must be labeled as exploratory.
Include the sample_01-excluded sensitivity results alongside, never as a replacement.
Use limma (moderated t, no covariates) as a complementary check on the logCPM-derived scores if desired, but the primary tests are the distribution-free and Welch tests above.
State method units in every table (score units vs fractions) so cross-method results are never mixed numerically.
acceptance_criteria: One results table per method: population, treated mean, control mean, effect size with 95% CI, raw p, BH-adjusted p, direction, and the sample_01-excluded versions of each.
A heatmap of z-scored per-sample composition annotated by treatment group, with sample_01 visibly flagged.

A concluding summary distinguishing (a) populations consistently changed across methods with effect-size support, (b) method-specific signals, and (c) no-difference populations — with the low-power caveat attached to (a) and (b).

plan.title: Anti-PD-1 vs isotype tumor immune-stromal deconvolution
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is mouse (Mus musculus) bulk RNA-seq of subcutaneous tumors: 12 samples, 6 anti-PD-1-treated vs 6 isotype-control, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level Salmon counts for 12,000 genes (counts.csv, 12000 x 13 with a gene-symbol ID column) plus a 12 x 2 metadata table. The question — what immune and stromal populations each sample contains and whether composition differs by treatment — is a bulk-tumor-microenvironment deconvolution problem, not a differential-expression problem. The plan therefore: (1) QC and normalize the counts (flagging sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median, which matters for compositional methods), (2) estimate per-sample immune and stromal cell composition with two independent mouse-compatible approaches that triangulate each other — mMCP-counter (mouse-specific immune + stromal population scores) and EPIC with the mouse TRef reference (absolute fractions incl. tumor cells, CAF, endothelial, macrophages), plus UCell marker-signature scoring of human TME signatures ortholog-projected to mouse — and (3) test treated-vs-control differences per population with effect sizes, multiple-testing correction, and a sensitivity analysis excluding the low-depth sample. With n=6 vs 6 the study is underpowered for small effects, so the statistics step reports effect sizes and CIs rather than leaning on p-values alone. No external reference download is required: mMCP-counter and EPIC/TRef ship their own mouse signatures, and the scGate human TME signature tables staged under /mnt/refs supply the marker sets for the third view.
